holidays.name: National Chewing Gum Day
holidays.description: Pop a stick, blow a bubble and give your jaw a little workout. This day celebrates the humble chewing gum in every flavor, from classic mint to fruity and fizzy.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a yearly excuse to celebrate one of the world's most popular chewable treats.
holidays.funFact: People have chewed gum for thousands of years. Archaeologists found a 5,700-year-old lump of birch tar in Denmark with tooth marks still in it.

holidays.name: Pet Tricks Day
holidays.description: Time to teach your dog to roll over, your cat to high-five or your parrot to say something embarrassing. It's a day for showing off your pet's talents and learning a new trick together.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. Pet lovers have adopted it as a playful reason to train, perform and share their animals' best stunts.
holidays.funFact: Many trainers teach tricks with positive reinforcement. Even a simple trick like 'spin' gives a pet mental exercise and strengthens your bond.

holidays.name: International Podcast Day
holidays.description: A global shout-out to the people who make and listen to podcasts. Whether you like true crime, comedy or niche hobby chats, today is for hitting play and finding a new favorite show.
holidays.origin: This is an international observance created by podcast fans and creators to celebrate the medium and its worldwide community.
holidays.funFact: The word 'podcast' was popularized in 2004 when journalist Ben Hammersley suggested it in The Guardian. It blends 'iPod' with 'broadcast'.
